itens.titulo: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) Shareholders Who Lost Money Have Opportunity to Lead Securities Fraud Lawsuit
itens.descricao: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) Shareholders Who Lost Money Have Opportunity to Lead Securities Fraud Lawsuit PR Newswire
itens.texto:
LOS ANGELES, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP announces that investors with losses have opportunity to lead the securities fraud class action lawsuit against Alphabet Inc.
IF YOU SUFFERED A LOSS ON YOUR ALPHABET INC. INVESTMENTS, CLICK HERE BEFORE DECEMBER 1, 2026 (LEAD PLAINTIFF DEADLINE) TO PARTICIPATE IN THE SECURITIES FRAUD LAWSUIT
What Is The Lawsuit About? 
The complaint filed in this class action alleges that between May 19, 2026 and July 16, 2026, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) that the Gemini 3.5 Pro was delivering disappointing training results; (2) that, as a result, the launch of Gemini 3.5 Pro would be significantly delayed; and (3) that, as a result of the foregoing, Defendants' positive statements about the Company's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.
What's The Next Step?
Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP is a leading national shareholder rights law firm, ready to assist you in potentially pursuing claims to recover your loss.
If you wish to serve as lead plaintiff, you must move the Court no later than December 1, 2026. Please contact us to learn more about your rights and interests by clicking here, by email ([email protected]), or by telephone at 310-201-9150 (Toll-Free: 888-773-9224).
You may retain counsel of your choice. If you bought securities during the class period, you may take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified yet.
Why Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP?
GPWR is a premier law firm with decades of experience representing investors and consumers in securities litigation and other complex class action litigation. Recognizing the firm's recent successes, GPWR was named one of Law360's Securities Groups of the Year and ranked 2nd in total investor recoveries by Institutional Shareholder Services Securities Class Action Services in 2025. GPWR's lawyers have handled cases covering a wide spectrum of corporate misconduct and relating to nearly all industries and sectors. GPWR's past successes have been widely covered by leading news and industry publications such as The Wall Street Journal, The Financial Times, Bloomberg Businessweek, Reuters, the Associated Press, Barron's, Investor's Business Daily, Forbes, and Money. Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.
This press release may be considered Attorney Advertising in some jurisdictions under the applicable law and ethical rules.

itens.titulo: Broadcom CEO Warns AI's Biggest Constraint Is Shifting
itens.descricao: Broadcom CEO Warns AI's Biggest Constraint Is Shifting Yahoo Finance
trechos: GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with AVGO.
The company is reportedly in early discussions to arrange more than $50 billion in debt financing to help OpenAI fund purchases of custom AI chips that the two companies are jointly developing.
Broadcom is also lending Anthropic as much as $42 billion to support infrastructure spending through a broader relationship involving computing equipment.
Reuters has reported that Anthropic could become Broadcom's largest chip-design customer in 2027.
There are also reports that Broadcom's Wall Street syndicate is beginning to arrange another $60 billion in AI-chip financing for Anthropic and other customers.

But if customers increasingly require tens of billions of dollars in financing simply to fund those purchases, growth becomes more dependent on credit markets, borrowing costs and investor willingness to keep supplying capital.

itens.descricao: 3 Reasons We’re Fans of Micron (MU) Yahoo Finance
trechos: Shares of the company have skyrocketed 141%, hitting $1,029.

Founded in the basement of a Boise, Idaho dental office in 1978, Micron (NASDAQ:MU) is a leading provider of memory chips used in thousands of devices across mobile, data centers, industrial, consumer, and automotive markets.
Thankfully, Micron's 36.9% annualized revenue growth over the last five years was incredible.
Micron's EPS grew at 65.6% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years, higher than its 36.9% annualized revenue growth.
The company's free cash flow margin was among the best in the semiconductor sector, averaging an eye-popping 35.5% over the last two years.

Final Judgment These are just a few reasons why we think Micron is one of the best semiconductor companies out there, and after the recent rally, the stock trades at 5.9× forward P/E (or $1,029 per share).

itens.titulo: Not Sandisk, Not Intel. This Stock Will Lead the S&P 500 Next Year
itens.descricao: Not Sandisk, Not Intel. This Stock Will Lead the S&P 500 Next Year Yahoo Finance
trechos: The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) has had a great year so far.
The average annual return of the S&P 500 is about 10%, and with it sitting at about 14.5% right now, it has been a good year.
While the S&P 500 as a whole is doing well, a few individual performers stand out.
Sandisk holds the title for best-performing S&P 500 stock this year, rising about 590% in 2026.
Intel is another top performer, increasing nearly 200% so far this year.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
Continue » So, which stock will lead the S&P 500 higher next year?
